evidence.quote: The general business law is amended by adding a new section

summary.short: Proposed New York bill S 934 would add section 399-zzzzzz to the General Business Law, requiring owners, licensees and operators of generative artificial intelligence systems to display a conspicuous notice that outputs may be inaccurate. Failure carries a civil penalty of up to one thousand dollars per violation, and the act takes effect on the ninetieth day after it becomes law.
summary.long: The bill adds section 399-zzzzzz to the New York General Business Law. It defines a generative artificial intelligence system as a class of self-supervised AI models that emulate the structure and characteristics of input data to generate derived synthetic content, such as images, videos, audio and text. It also defines artificial intelligence broadly as machine-based systems that make predictions, recommendations or decisions for human-defined objectives. Under subdivision 2, the owner, licensee or operator of a generative AI system must clearly and conspicuously display a notice on the system's user interface that the system's outputs may be inaccurate. Under subdivision 3, an owner, licensee or operator that fails to provide this notice is assessed a civil penalty of up to one thousand dollars for each violation, and each user to whom the notice is not provided constitutes a separate violation. The text does not name the authority that assesses the penalty and does not address a private right of action or a cure period. Section 2 provides that the act takes effect on the ninetieth day after it becomes law. The document is bill text and states no legislative history.

relations.note: The bill adds a new section 399-zzzzzz to the General Business Law. No other relations are stated in the text.

notes: Introduced bill text; no consolidated version available. Subdivision 3 contains garbled wording ('EACH USER THE OWNER, LICENSEE OR OPERATOR FAILS TO PROVIDE A NOTICE TO SHALL CONSTITUTE A SEPARATE VIOLATION FOR EACH INSTANCE'), so the unit of violation (per user or per instance) is unclear and is recorded as written. The text names no enforcing authority and says nothing about a private right of action or cure period. Subdivision 1(B) defines 'artificial intelligence' broadly, but the operative notice duty in subdivision 2 uses only the 1(A) term 'generative artificial intelligence system'.

thresholds.note: The bill has no numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment. It applies to every owner, licensee or operator of a generative AI system without size or user-count tests. The only figures are the civil penalty ceiling of one thousand dollars per violation in subdivision 3, which is recorded under enforcement, and the ninetieth-day effective date in section 2, which is recorded as an event.
